title: Your heart never takes a day off
body: The human heart beats about 100,000 times every day and pumps thousands of litres of blood around your body.

title: Babies have more bones than adults
body: A baby is born with about 300 soft bones and cartilage pieces. As they grow, many fuse together, and an adult has 206 bones.

title: Your brain is an energy hog
body: Your brain is only about 2% of your body weight, but it uses roughly 20% of your energy, even while you sleep.

title: Tooth enamel: the hardest part of you
body: The shiny outside of your teeth, enamel, is the hardest substance in the human body. But it cannot grow back, so brushing and avoiding too much sugar really matter.

title: Blood cells have a short life
body: A red blood cell lives about 120 days. Your body makes millions of new ones every second in the bone marrow.

title: No two fingerprints are the same
body: Fingerprints form before birth. Even identical twins, who share the same DNA, have different fingerprints.

title: Your small intestine is about 6 metres long
body: The small intestine is about 6 metres long when stretched out. It is packed into your belly in neat folds and loops.

title: The smallest bone in your body
body: The stapes, deep inside your ear, is about 3 millimetres long. It helps carry sound to the inner ear.

title: Skin: your biggest organ
body: Your skin is the largest organ of your body. It protects you from germs, helps control your temperature and gives you your sense of touch.

title: Why you need to sleep
body: During sleep your brain sorts and stores what you learned during the day. Learners who sleep enough usually remember more and concentrate better.

title: You are mostly water
body: Water makes up about 60% of an adult’s body weight, and even more in babies. Drinking enough keeps your body and brain working well.
